evidence: Cic. Tusc. 4.34: hujus virtūtis contrāria est vitiōsitās (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The neuter of contrārius, opposite, which takes a genitive or a dative. Ex contrāriō (Nepos ē contrāriō) is “on the contrary, conversely”; in contrārium, into the reverse.

terms.gloss: on the contrary, the other way
terms.comment: Sets one clause against another; as an answer that denies what was said, immō (see actually).
For going backwards, as a car in reverse: retrō agere, to drive it back.

phrases.latin: Immō contrā: ille mē pulsāvit, nōn ego illum.
phrases.english: No, the other way round: he hit me, not I him.

sources: Lewis & Short: contrarius · Lewis & Short: contra · Lewis & Short: retro
The example sentences marked “composed” are ours.
